title: LindenWorks partner prospect scout - raw
content:
Summary:
Quick research + outbound plan for LindenWorks (mid-market SaaS, vertical: facilities management + tenant experience). Goal: secure a 6-week pilot to validate embedded LLM for tenant support and automated maintenance ticket triage. 

Why LindenWorks might care (hypothesis):
- Heavy inbound support volume (property managers + tenants). Potential to reduce manual touch by automated triage & templated responses.
- Security/data residency is a blocker for their enterprise customers — they ask about private deployments.
- Need predictable cost and latency during peak move-in/move-out windows.

Key contacts (to build):
- Head of Platform / VP Engineering (primary technical champ) — likely to care about deployment model (VPC/private), SDKs, integration points (webhooks, message bus).
- Head of Customer Experience / Support Ops (ROI champion) — cares about reduction in ticket volume, deflection %, MTTR.
- Product Manager (owner of roadmap) — cares about experiments, quick A/B tests, quality/regression monitoring.
- Security/compliance lead (procurement gate) — will ask about KMS, audit logs, SOC2/ISO, and private control plane.

Public signals / data points:
- Job postings in last 6 months: platform engineer, senior infra — scaling focus. (source: LinkedIn snapshot 2026-01)
- Blog post (2025-11): "Improving onsite turnaround for tenant requests" — mentions manual categorization of requests and a roadmap item to explore NLP.
- G2 reviews mention slow support during peak season and frequent ticket misclassification.

Initial qualification questions to ask on discovery call:
- Volume: What is your current monthly ticket volume (and % coming from tenants vs managers)? Any seasonality?
- Latency/SLAs: What are your current support SLAs? What p95 latency would you accept for an automated assist?
- Data: Are inbound messages PII-heavy? Do customers require data residency / on-prem / VPC?
- Integrations: Which support systems do you use (Zendesk, Intercom, ServiceNow)? Any message bus (Kafka) or event streams?
- Success metrics: What would a successful 6-week pilot look like (deflection %, triage accuracy, developer hours saved)?

Value props to surface (tailored):
- Predictable pilot: Redwood Private (VPC) + 6-week runbook — gives security and audit trail needed for procurement.
- Rapid iterations: quick SDKs + example connectors for Zendesk/Intercom to reduce integration time (2–3 dev days).
- Cost control: proposed cap and intelligent batching to control per-token spend during spikes.
- Observability: token-level cost and accuracy dashboards to show ROI in pilot.

Outreach sequence (multithreaded):
1) Short cold email to Head of Platform (focus: security + technical proof): subject: "Pilot: private LLM triage for LindenWorks — 6-week plan". Body: 3 bullets (who we are, quick value, ask for 20m to show demo + pilot plan).
2) LinkedIn connection + one-liner referencing mutual signals (blog post).
3) If no response in 4 days -> intro to Support Ops with an angle on cost savings & sample metrics.
4) Send a one-pager with pilot scope + SLOs + SOW stub.

Email draft (short) — TO HEAD OF PLATFORM:
Hi <Name>,
Quick note — I saw LindenWorks' post about improving tenant turnaround and thought you might be a fit for a short private LLM pilot we run with companies in proptech. We deploy in a VPC, connect to Zendesk/Intercom, and show token-level cost + accuracy within 6 weeks.
Would you be open to 20 minutes next week to review a pilot runbook and sample integration?
Thanks,
Maya Chen (Redwood)

Call script highlights / discovery checklist:
- 5 min: intros and context (mention VPC/private option up front).
- 10 min: volume, systems, security requirements (collect exact answers).
- 5 min: show quick sample of triage + fallback behavior (on demo call use canned dataset).
- Close: agree pilot success metrics and timeline.

Objection handling (expected):
1) "We can build this ourselves":
  - Acknowledge: "Totally — your team knows the domain best."
  - Response: "Pilot is engineered to minimize lift: we provide a connector + runbook, and you keep control. Aim is to prove ROI in 6 weeks; if results are good, you can either continue with Redwood or take learnings in-house."
2) "Data privacy / compliance":
  - Close with specifics: private control plane option, KMS integration, audit logs, SOC2 + option for on-prem packaging. Offer to set up a security call with our compliance engineer (Priya).
3) "Cost unpredictability":
  - Response: propose a capped pilot budget + batching/quantization knobs. Share sample cost model (tokens/day -> estimated monthly cost at p50/p95).
4) "Model hallucinations / accuracy":
  - Response: show eval hooks, prompt set based regression detection, ability to pin model versions and fallback to simpler rerankers. Propose guardrails: confidence thresholds + human-in-the-loop for low-confidence items.

Pilot proposal (6-week, high level):
- Week 0: Kickoff, access & security onboarding, selection of 2–3 support flows (e.g., password resets, move-in maintenance triage).
- Week 1–2: Connector work (Zendesk/Intercom), sample dataset ingestion, prompt engineering.
- Week 3: Shadow mode (suggestions visible to agents), metrics baseline collection.
- Week 4–5: Gradual automation (30% -> 60% of suggested workflows) + monitoring dashboards.
- Week 6: Wrap, outcomes report, recommended next steps (Dedicated reserved capacity? Private contract?).
Deliverables:
- Integration connectors + runbook.
- Pilot SLO dashboard (accuracy, deflection, cost).
- Security artifact pack (audit logs, KMS setup notes).

Success metrics (example):
- 20–30% ticket deflection for low-complexity requests.
- Triage accuracy >= 85% on selected flows.
- p95 latency for suggestions < 400ms in pilot configuration.
- Developer time saved: 2 FTE-months equivalent over pilot cadence (tracked via agent time reduction).

Pricing guardrails (pilot):
- Flat pilot fee: $18k (covers integration + 6 weeks runtime up to capped token budget).
- Overage: negotiated per-token after cap, or option to pause.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Confirm whether LindenWorks uses Zendesk or Intercom (website hints at Zendesk but not certain). TODO: lookup freshest integrations in their help center.
- Get link to their security questionnaire (SaaS procurement docs). Ask Priya to prep answers & SOC2 pack.
- Create a canned dataset of 200 sample tenant messages we can use for demo (ask solutions-eng to synthesize).
- Check with infra eng: can we guarantee p95 < 400ms on Private for their expected scale? If not, propose Dedicated baseline and adjust SLO.

Next steps (immediate):
- [Today] Send cold email to Head of Platform (Gabe to review).
- [+2d] Post follow-up message on LinkedIn if no response.
- [This week] Draft pilot SOW stub to attach in follow-up. (Priya owns SOW draft.)

Last thought: keep ask specific and small — pilot must be low friction. Emphasize security and observability (that's what will unlock procurement).

--END--
